sentences.text: Protopteryx is an extinct bird from the Cretaceous period and is possibly the most basal member of the Enantiornithes group.
Fossils indicate the animal was roughly the size of a modern starling.
It possessed conical, unserrated teeth, some of which possessed a resorption pit similar to those found in Archaeopteryx.
The barbs of its down feathers were laminar rather than hairlike and were frayed at the tips.
The most distinctive feature was a tail consisting of two long feathers that only had barbs at their tips.
The name Protopteryx means "primitive feather", derived from Greek roots meaning "first" and "feather" or "wing".
Protopteryx was first discovered in Hebei Province, northern China, dating from 131 million years ago.
It is known from a nearly complete articulated holotype skeleton found in the Sichakou Member of the Huajiying Formation in Hebei Province, China, dating to about 131 million years ago.
Protopteryx was adapted for flying, possessing features like a carina of the sternum and deltoid crest that suggest it had modern flight muscles.
It shared asymmetric wing flight feathers with flying birds, Archaeopteryx, and Confuciusornis.
The lack of barbs and rami on the proximal part of Protopteryx's tail feathers suggests they were used for display, thermoregulation, or sensory functions rather than flight.
Protopteryx appeared after Archaeopteryx and Confuciusornis in the evolutionary timeline.
Protopteryx lived in the Jehol Biota during the Cretaceous period, an environment containing many terrestrial and freshwater vertebrate groups.
Protopteryx lived during the Hauterivian to Barremian stages, from 132.6 to 121.4 million years ago.
